Games Action Games Grand Theft Auto GTA 6 Nearly 1 in 3 gamers plan to buy GTA 6 in the US, analyst confirms: "A rare cultural and commercial moment" News By Anna Koselke Published 28 October 2026 "Players have been waiting 13 years for a sequel to Grand Theft Auto 5" When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here's how it works . (Image credit: Rockstar) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The GTA 6 release is quickly approaching, and it's set to be one of the biggest video game releases of all time - so big, in fact, that analysts say nearly one in three gamers is looking to indulge in Rockstar's long-awaited sixth Grand Theft Auto entry. That's a hefty figure... one that comes straight from global market research and consumer behavior advisor Circana, along with commentary from veteran analyst and company lead Mat Piscatella. To be more precise, it's 29% - a good 29% of gamers in the United States, both on console and PC, intend to purchase GTA 6. This number marks Rockstar's game as the most-ever anticipated video game release in Circana's tracking history. "Grand Theft Auto 6 represents a rare cultural and commercial moment for the video game industry," Piscatella writes. "Players have been waiting 13 years for a sequel to Grand Theft Auto 5, and demand is expected to extend beyond software sales to include consoles, accessories, and gaming subscriptions as consumers prepare for launch." It's wild to think about, really. GTA 6 won't just sell a plethora of game copies, either. It'll also sell consoles. "Many consumers who have yet to upgrade to a current-generation console may choose to purchase a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series specifically to play the title," as Piscatella notes - and this applies to folks who otherwise game on PC, too, as Rockstar won't be releasing GTA 6 on computer storefronts just yet . Put simply, it'll spur a whole lot of buying and consuming, both in the software and hardware department. Latest Videos From GamesRadar+ Watch full video here: "As retailers prepare for Black Friday and holiday season demand, Grand Theft Auto 6 will be a major driver of software sales, hardware upgrades, and gaming-related tech purchases throughout the fourth quarter," Piscatella concludes. "Its anticipation and popularity reinforces the growing influence of video games on the broader entertainment and consumer technology markets." Boy, does it. Interestingly, as huge and influential as GTA 6 evidently is, Piscatella recently said that devs shouldn't "fear" launching around Rockstar's behemoth , since many people "are going to want to play other things," too. I suppose he's not wrong on that end either, though - there's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , for instance, and a handful of other nice November releases to look forward to. Managing to draw nearly one in three gamers, whether primarily on console or PC, is no small feat, after all - especially when you consider how big the American market is in particular.
